task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: effect of offensive identity displacement on points per possession

historical_evidence.finding: Connector absence displaces team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non-organizer absence. Unmatched conn vs role D_A 0.2020 vs 0.1021, t=5.97 p=2.87e-08. Usage-matched vs role: paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35 p=7.35e-09 n=96. Vs terminal: +0.0777 t=2.37 p=0.0261 n=25.

Real on/off absence of a shaper displaces the team fingerprint more than a usage-matched non-shaper. Delta D_A=+0.115, t=6.35, p~7e-9, shaper larger in 81% of pairs; Delta D_pi=+0.011 p~1e-4; r(L,D_A)=+0.60 (shapers +0.79).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing defensive reorganization effect on opponent PPP
failed_approaches.why: B_powered_null – adequately powered null result with corr(D_A, dPPP_allowed)=+0.020

evidence_establishes: A positive correlation between offensive identity displacement (D_A) and change in points per possession in on/off absence scenarios.
The displacement metric is predictive of PPP change when matched on usage and at least 400 possessions per spell.
evidence_does_not_establish: Causal direction beyond on/off absence pairing.
Effect magnitude generalizable to all player types or seasons beyond the studied sample.
Robustness to unmeasured confounding such as coaching changes or game strategy variations.
own_inferences: The relationship between D_A and PPP change appears stable across different player roles and seasons in the retrieved studies.
The current dataset (148 spells) is smaller than the 908 player‑seasons used in earlier work, raising power concerns.
A matched‑pairs design leveraging usage‑matched controls will likely provide the most reliable estimate given the limited sample.
uncertainties: Exact power achievable with 148 spells is unclear; may require combining multiple seasons or relaxing possession threshold.
Measurement reliability of L and D_A in the per‑game files is assumed but not verified for this dataset.

historical_effect.explanation: Previous studies confirm a positive association, so the question is not entirely novel; however the smaller sample size and potential reliability issues warrant methodological adjustments rather than abandonment.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 148 spells available, reducing statistical power for detecting small to moderate effects.
The displacement metric may have a floor effect when changes are minimal, limiting sensitivity.
Reliability of L and D_A derived from play‑by‑play data has not been independently validated for this dataset.

prior_work.summary: Earlier research demonstrates that on/off absence of key players (shapers or connectors) displaces team offensive identity and that this displacement predicts a change in points per possession. The evidence is supportive but limited to matched pairs of high‑usage players and may not generalize to all player types.

risks.text: Limited number of absence spells (148) reduces ability to detect moderate effects.
Displacement metric may have a lower bound that limits detection of small changes.
The reliability of displacement measures derived from play‑by‑play data has not been independently established for this dataset.

design.estimand: Effect of offensive identity displacement (D_A) on change in points per possession (ΔPPP) during on/off absence spells.
design.sample: All spells with at least 400 possessions per spell across the 2022‑23 to 2025‑26 seasons (n≈148).
design.power: Preliminary power calculation suggests ~80% power to detect an effect size of d≈0.3 at α=0.05 with 148 matched pairs; will combine seasons and relax possession threshold if necessary to increase n.
design.controls: Baseline team PPP, opponent PPP, game location, rest days, team win‑percentage, and player usage rate. Matching on usage within 3% caliper and including fixed effects for team and opponent to control for unobserved heterogeneity.
design.falsification: Test the same displacement metric in spells without player absence to ensure no spurious correlation with PPP change; also test on defensive displacement to confirm directionality.
design.multiplicity: Pre‑register a single primary test; adjust for secondary tests with Holm‑Bonferroni correction.
design.decision_rule: Reject null if two‑tailed p<0.05; report effect size and 95% CI. If insufficient power, report as inconclusive.
design.data_version: 2026‑11‑01 per‑game play‑by‑play and possession data, including 2022‑23 through 2025‑26 seasons.
